unit.can_do_en: say I don't understand and ask someone to repeat or slow down.

brief.situation_en: Maria at a shop checkout. Kari speaks fast.

lines.speaker: Kari
lines.text_puhe: Haluuksä muovipussin vai onks sul oma kassi?
lines.text_kirja: Haluatko sinä muovipussin vai onko sinulla oma kassi?
lines.gloss_en: Do you want a plastic bag or do you have your own bag?

judge.reason: Same question: plastic bag or own bag; only register differs (haluuk, onks, sul).

puhe.text: Haluuksä muovipussin vai onks sul oma kassi?

kirja.text: Haluatko sinä muovipussin vai onko sinulla oma kassi?

judge.reason: Same: sorry, I didn't understand; spoken forms only.
Same question: do you want a bag; register difference only.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Could you speak a bit more slowly?

judge.reason: Same: can you speak a bit slower; spoken 'voit sä puhuu' equals 'voitko sinä puhua'.

lines.speaker: Kari
lines.gloss_en: Of course. Do you need a bag?

judge.reason: Same: do you need a bag; tarviitko is spoken form of tarvitsetko.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Ai, pussin! Ei kiitos, mul on oma.
lines.text_kirja: Ai, pussin! Ei kiitos, minulla on oma.
lines.gloss_en: Oh, a bag! No thanks, I have my own.

judge.reason: Same: no thanks, I have my own; mul = minulla.

puhe.text: Ai, pussin! Ei kiitos, mul on oma.

kirja.text: Ai, pussin! Ei kiitos, minulla on oma.

lines.speaker: Kari
lines.text_puhe: Hyvä. Sä puhut jo hyvin suomee.
lines.text_kirja: Hyvä. Sinä puhut jo hyvin suomea.
lines.gloss_en: Good. You already speak Finnish well.

judge.reason: Same: you already speak Finnish well; suomee = suomea.

puhe.text: Hyvä. Sä puhut jo hyvin suomee.

kirja.text: Hyvä. Sinä puhut jo hyvin suomea.

judge.reason: Same: thanks, I'm still learning; kiitti = kiitos, mä = minä.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: In Haluuksä, speech says haluu for haluat and -k for -ko, then joins sä.
Speech shortens sinä to sä. Books write sinä.
Muovipussi with -n when you take the whole thing: muovipussin.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: On with -ko to ask a question. Speech often says -ks: onks.
Sinä with -lla. With on it means 'you have'. Speech shortens it to sul.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech drops the final i: anteeksi becomes anteeks.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Ei with -n for 'I': en, I do not.
After en, 'I don't', a past action uses this form: en ymmärtänyt. Speech drops the last t: ymmärtäny.
Pussi with -n when you take the whole thing: pussin.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Voit with -ko asks 'can you?': voitko. Speech drops -ko and adds sä: voitsä.
Puhua in its basic form after voitko. Speech turns -ua into -uu.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Hidas, slow, becomes hitaammin, 'more slowly'. The d turns to t and -mmin means 'more'.
From tosi, true. Totta kai means of course.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Tarvitset, you need, with -ko to ask. Speech says tarviitko.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Ei on its own answers 'no'. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Minä with -lla. With on it means 'I have'. Speech shortens it to mul.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Puhua, to speak, with -t for 'you': puhut.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The partitive adds -a after puhua, to speak: suomea. Speech turns -ea into -ee.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.
Opetella, to learn, with -n for 'I': opettelen.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
